before.title: mk_list_add is declared borrowed on both positions, so a Monkey object linked into a caller-reachable list is still accused at the next exit (8 leaves)
before.why: providers/qcore-provider-libevent/contracts/monkey/intrusive_list.qcore declares mk_list_add(entry, head) resource_borrowed on both parameters. Linking `&obj->_head` into a list reachable from the caller publishes `obj`, which a borrowed position does not state, so card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT's audit found 8 class (c) leak leaves in 7 functions whose accusation rests on that silence (mk_rconf_meta_add, mk_rconf_read, mk_rconf_section_entry_add, mk_sched_worker_cb_add, mk_vhost_set_property, mk_vhost_set_single 2, mk_vhost_create 1); reading shows each object linked into its caller's configuration, server or host. Discharge condition: a vocabulary or contract that states an intrusive insertion's publication of the containing object (the v1 `resource_stored` relation over an interior address, or an equivalent), with gateway and Lean parity, and an arbiter attributing each withdrawn leaf. After the refused hand-on rule, 5 of the 8 are also withdrawn (the object is named in a refused statement on the path); 3 stay published (mk_vhost_create, mk_vhost_set_property, mk_vhost_set_single).
